title: Why I Started Growing Minds
excerpt: Hi, I'm Peter. Growing Minds began with podcasts, dinner on the stove and stories made up for my kids. Here's how it started.
body:
By Peter, founder of Growing Minds

I'm the dad of an eight year old son and a five year old daughter. I started Growing Minds because I wanted stories that were about my kids, and that quietly helped them with whatever they were working on. Here's how it began, and a few things my kids taught me along the way.

Hi, I'm Peter, and I made Growing Minds.

How did Growing Minds start?

It started with podcasts. My kids and I love listening to them together. And when I say love, I mean they were totally obsessed. It was also a nice way for me to get a little free time to cook.

A lot of what we listened to was things like the Frozen stories and the Dragon Master books, on repeat for what felt like years. I tried to find educational ones too. We went all in on Who, When, Wow! and Wow in the World. (I hear "can we listen to Carly Q?" at least three times per day.) Then we ran out of episodes, and I couldn't find enough options to keep up with my kids' appetite. So we played them again and again, until my kids were talking along word for word.

So I started asking AI to write stories about each of my kids. Then I'd have Siri read them out loud while I cooked. Everybody got a story, and I got to keep stirring. The stories were pretty awful, and Siri is terrible at reading, but my kids were hooked anyway.

Soon I started working in lessons they were learning in real life. How to say sorry to a sibling. How brave it is to get back on your bike after you've fallen off. Sometimes they noticed the idea I'd snuck in, and sometimes they didn't. Either way, I could pause the audio, we'd talk about what they'd heard, and we could try it out in real life.

Then came the books. Reading and cuddling before bed is my favorite part of the day, and my kids will happily tell you so. They're calm, they're curious, and I get to just feel them next to me. I know there's plenty of research about reading before bed, and that's great. Honestly though, I just love how it makes us all feel.

So I started printing their stories as books at the copy store. My son would take his to his room and read it on his own after we all read together. My daughter stayed on my lap and listened to hers.

That's how Growing Minds was born. That and a lot of trial and error.

What did my kids teach me about stories?

Quite a lot, actually. Some of what we found came straight from my kids.

They can spot a fake. If a story adds a person my kids are supposed to know, but the character is made up, they look at me and shake their heads with a knowing smile. Busted. Kids know their own world really well.

They love the pictures. The audio stories had no pictures, and the first printouts didn't have many either. But my kids would explode with joy when they saw themselves as a character in the story. Seeing themselves talk to unicorns, or get a magical letter from a wizard school, blew their minds. So I wanted to make sure they got as many images as I could fit into each story.

They love a fantasy. My kids loved to hear any story about themselves, but the fantasy stories added an extra something. It gave them a world in which they got to do magical things, and it made their imaginations really rejoice.

And here's one I noticed on my own.

Every story should lift them up. Every time I make a story, I want to make sure it lifts my kids up. In our house, we talk a lot about Brené Brown's candle idea. The basic idea is that each person has an inner candle. It's our job to light other people's candles, not blow them out. And it's our job to spot the people who blow candles out, and adjust accordingly. I want our books to light the flame in our kids, and in everyone's. If we could make that happen, what a win that would be.

Where is Growing Minds now?

Growing Minds is the grown-up version of those dinner-time stories: a personalized illustrated chapter book where your child is the hero, built around what they're working on right now, like starting school, making friends or managing big feelings.

We're getting ready to launch, and we're working hard to get the stories just right for each kid. We'd love to help light your child's candle, and help them with what they're working on along the way. The waitlist is open. If you have questions, email help@growingminds.io and I'll get right back to you.
